items.title: New Indian envoy calls on Nepal’s foreign minister
items.desc: Ambassador Sudhakar Dalela meets Shisir Khanal at Singha Durbar and discusses the longstanding ties between the two countries.

items.title: Four killed as auto-rickshaw plunges off road in Bajhang
items.desc: The vehicle carrying six people fell 900 metres down a slope after its brakes reportedly failed. Police have taken the driver into custody for investigation.

items.title: Bhutanese rights groups urge Shah to raise refugee issue with India
items.desc: They want the prime minister to press Narendra Modi to help resolve the decades-old refugee crisis, secure the release of political prisoners and address human rights violations in Bhutan.

items.title: Nepal’s ambassadors to India, China and Israel take oath
items.desc: The three were among ten ambassadorial nominees approved by the Parliamentary Hearing Committee after the Cabinet recommended 13 appointments in September.

items.title: Deleted from India’s voter rolls, some Muslims face detention, deportation
items.desc: A voter-roll revision has become entangled with a wider crackdown on suspected undocumented migrants.

items.title: Night travel restricted on Hetauda-Kathmandu road via Bhimphedi
items.desc: The move follows a fatal crash that killed 14 people last week, with authorities citing the narrow, winding and poorly lit road as a major accident risk.

items.title: Six wild elephants die in two months, raising conservation concerns
items.desc: From Chitwan to eastern Nepal, a series of elephant deaths has alarmed conservationists, who warn that shrinking habitats, human activities and unsafe migration routes could threaten the country’s wild elephant population.

items.title: Chhath concludes with offerings to rising sun
items.desc: Devotees gather on the banks of the Bagmati river in Thapathali, Kathmandu, to perform the final rituals of the four-day festival and pray for their families’ well-being.

items.title: UML puts local, provincial elections at centre of national gathering
items.desc: The party plans to mobilise its organisation for the upcoming polls while stepping up public outreach, defending democratic institutions and reshaping its political agenda.

items.title: Qatar’s economic slump puts Nepali workers’ jobs at risk
items.desc: New labour approvals for Qatar have fallen by 35 percent since the war began, while rising complaints of layoffs and delayed wages point to growing pressure on Nepali workers already employed there.

items.title: Law students challenge use of AI detectors to brand academic work as plagiarism
items.desc: A writ petition argues that AI use and plagiarism must be treated as distinct issues, warning that decisions based solely on AI-detection software could unfairly damage students’ academic careers.

items.title: Nepal’s stolen Uma-Maheshvara statues belong back in their shrines
items.desc: Returning stolen statues to the country is only the first step. They should be in the shrines where generations worshipped them.

items.title: Things to do in Kathmandu Valley this week
items.desc: From creative workshops and writing circles to European cinema and cricket, Kathmandu Valley has plenty to offer this week.

items.title: Nepal, India to launch Ayodhya-Janakpur train service during PM Shah’s visit
items.desc: The weekly service will initially run on an Indian train. Kathmandu is also preparing to seek New Delhi’s grant assistance to electrify the 28-kilometre stretch of railway in Nepal.

items.title: Dalit devotees face caste segregation at Chhath celebration in Madhesh
items.desc: Separate ghats and tents in Saptari and Rautahat expose the gap between the festival’s message of equality and the discrimination that persists despite constitutional guarantees and laws against caste-based discrimination.

items.title: Why did Nepal’s mountain agenda stall at COP31? A delegation insider explains
items.desc: Environment Minister’s adviser says the real contest at COP31 is now over the wording of the cover decision.

items.title: Rs43,500 is new minimum monthly wage for public project workers, twice the private-sector rate
items.desc: A new public procurement guideline guarantees higher pay and social security contributions for workers employed in government-funded projects, but contractors and labour suppliers say the rule came without consultation or cost analysis.

items.title: Attorney general’s office claims flaws in court verdicts on 33.5 kg gold smuggling case
items.desc: The attorney general’s office argues that the courts focused on the murder of Sanam Shakya but failed to examine the alleged smuggling network, organised crime and customs offences.

items.title: Why reforming business climate is vital to keeping youths home
items.desc: Many young people have pinned their hopes on this government; it cannot afford to disappoint them.

items.title: Why drying Madhesh is a disaster in the making
items.desc: Climate change is triggering multiple disasters simultaneously across the country, yet some remain far less visible than others.

items.title: Kathmandu to face Chitwan in NPL Eliminator after loss to Pokhara
items.desc: Kathmandu finish third with a 55-run defeat, while Kushal Bhurtel misses a century by one run as Pokhara post a record 224.

items.title: SpaceX Starship returns to landing pad from orbit, acing test for reusable rockets
items.desc: The spacecraft completed a 22-hour orbital flight before being caught by mechanical arms at its Texas launch tower, marking a major step towards SpaceX’s goal of developing fully reusable rockets.

items.title: Three dead, two injured in Mugu jeep crash
items.desc: The jeep plunged about 600 metres off the road in Chhayanath Rara Municipality while travelling from Surkhet to Rara.

items.title: Nepal sets up accreditation centre to ease testing and certification
items.desc: The agency aims to reduce testing costs, strengthen quality assurance and help Nepali products gain international recognition, but exporters say it could take up to three years to secure global accreditation.

items.title: Bhurtel falls one run short as Pokhara post record NPL total
items.desc: Kushal Bhurtel hits 99 off 51 balls as Pokhara Avengers pile up 224 for three against Kathmandu Gorkhas, the highest total in the competition’s history.

items.title: Changing farming practices threaten food and habitats of migratory birds
items.desc: The expansion of winter crops, shrinking wetlands, and rising use of pesticide are putting the survival of thousands of birds arriving in Nepal from Tibet, Mongolia, and Siberia at risk.

items.title: India approves weekly train service linking Janakpur and Ayodhya
items.desc: The 604-km cross-border service will connect two major Ramayana pilgrimage destinations, with stops in Bihar and Uttar Pradesh. The launch date and fares are yet to be announced.

items.title: Karnali sign off with consolation win as Chitwan finish fourth
items.desc: The Rhinos, already through to the playoffs, end the league stage on seven points after falling 24 runs short of a 154-run target.
